title: The doctor measures what the layout costs instead of guessing
description: F468 (field report 14): a phase-count threshold is a proxy; the cost is conflicted merges, replayed with git merge-tree without the driver.
desiredOutcome: doctor reports, from the repository's own merges, how many conflicted in the manifest without the driver, and warns with the install command when that number is not zero and the driver is absent
summary: Every task of this phase finished before a phase's status was derived. It was closed afterwards, when phase sign-off became a recorded verdict (P63), and no sign-off review ran at that close - so the verdict is skipped, and what this phase did is recorded by its tasks' commits and outcomes, not attested here.

tasks.title: Replay the repository's merges without the driver and count the ones that conflicted in the plan
tasks.description: Of the recent merges where both sides changed the plan, how many conflicted in it with git's own line merge (merge-tree --write-tree, the driver swapped for git merge-file). The doctor's merge-driver line reports it and warns, with the install command, when it is not zero and the driver is absent.

outcome.technical: _merge_install.replay_merges via merge-tree with git merge-file as the driver; reported on every merge-driver row; WARNING when paid for and not installed.
outcome.descriptive: The doctor tells a team, from its own merge history, how many merges conflicted in the plan and that the driver would have merged them.

tasks.title: In-place edit targets are the file operands, not tokens inside the script (F472)
tasks.description: The in-place write targets were harvested by a path-shaped regex over the whole clause, script included, so a covered stream-editor call whose substitution mentions a file name was refused as a write to that name - a guard firing on text it only mentions, the route-around class. Driven three times on 2026-09-24, the third being this very task's own add command, whose description quoted such a call. Parse the operands with each tool's own grammar, and read a clause without crossing into a quoted argument.

outcome.technical: sed and perl/ruby -i operand grammars, quote-aware clause detection and end, a tokenizer on the shared quote walk, wider harvest kept as the fallback.
outcome.descriptive: The shell-write guard no longer refuses a write to a file a command only mentions.
The CHANGELOG records the guard fix.
